blocks.text: I can describe the formation of sedimentary rock and suggest information that can be obtained from its layers.

items.title: Forming sedimentary rocks
items.sub: From loose sediment to solid rock

blocks.text: Tap each word to see what it means.

items.def: A material deposited by water, wind or ice, such as pebbles, sand, or salts left by evaporation.
The process of sediment grains settling out (being deposited) from water or wind as their flow slows, or as ice melts.
A process where sediment grains become compacted (squashed closer together) during burial.
A process by which sediment grains are cemented (stuck together) by minerals deposited from groundwater, turning the sediment into rock.
Layers of rock (several rock beds) formed by the deposition of sediment.

blocks.text: Over many years, rock on Earth's surface is weathered by biological, chemical or physical processes.
The weakened or broken rock can be eroded, which means transported to a new location. Wind, glaciers and rivers or streams can all do this.
Faster flowing wind or water can transport **more** and **larger** rock fragments. Slower flowing wind or water can only move **smaller, lighter** fragments.

items.q: Which is more likely to carry many large rock fragments a long way?
A slow flowing stream can mainly carry...
Which of these can move bits of rock or sand to another place?

blocks.text: When wind or water slows down, the rock fragments it is carrying are dropped.

items.title: Wind slows
items.sub: when it hits an obstruction, such as trees or mountains

items.title: Water slows
items.sub: when it flows across flatter land

items.title: Glaciers melt
items.sub: and drop the rock fragments they carried

blocks.text: Material dropped like this is called {sediment}. Sediments are small grains, and they can be made of many types of material:
The process of dropping sediments is called {deposition}.
Over time, deposition builds up layers of different sediments on top of each other.
The weight of the upper layers exerts pressure on the layers below. It is a bit like being at the bottom of a rugby pile!
This increasing pressure causes the sediments to undergo {compaction}. Compaction pushes sediment grains closer together and squeezes out groundwater that may be between the grains.

blocks.label: Which layer is compacted the least?
blocks.text: The layer with the fewest layers above it. Less weight means less pressure, so lower compaction.

blocks.q: In a stack of sediment layers, which layer feels the greatest pressure?
options: The top layer, with nothing above it
The bottom layer, with the most layers above it
All layers feel the same pressure
blocks.why: The weight of the upper layers presses on the layers below, so the layer with the most layers above it is compacted the most.

blocks.text: Water in nature always contains minerals. Minerals are crystal-like substances, such as quartz or calcite.
Groundwater moving between sediment grains can deposit these minerals in the pores, which are the spaces between the grains.
The increased pressure (and temperature) in a compacted layer gives the conditions for mineral crystals to form in the pores.
The mineral crystals act like {glue}, sticking the sediment grains together. This is called {cementation}. A sedimentary rock is now formed.

blocks.q: Are these about compaction or about cementation?

items.text: Caused by the pressure of the layers above
Squashes the sediment grains closer together
Mineral crystals grow in the pores
Acts like a glue between the grains
Minerals deposited from groundwater stick the grains together

slides.title: The journey from sediment to rock

blocks.text: There are many steps to making a sedimentary rock:

items: Weathering and erosion of existing rocks

blocks.text: Because there are so many steps, the process takes **millions of years**. The oldest sedimentary rocks in the UK were formed from sand sediments deposited 1000 million years ago.
All sedimentary rocks form by the same processes, but different sediments form different sedimentary rocks.
Some sedimentary rocks form from the remains of living organisms:

slides.title: Match the sediment to its rock

blocks.q: Match each sediment to the sedimentary rock it forms.

blocks.text: Sedimentary rocks form in layers. One layer is a {stratum}. Many layers are {strata}.
Upper strata were deposited after (later than) lower strata. So the position of each stratum helps to build a **relative timeline**.

items.title: Upper stratum
items.sub: recent deposition, so anything found there is from the recent past

items.title: Lower stratum
items.sub: earlier deposition, so anything found there is from the distant past

blocks.text: Scientists study strata to gain information about the past. Objects found in each stratum help build an understanding of the organisms that lived at that time.
Strata also give clues to past environments:

items.title: Cross-beds
items.sub: form due to shifts in sediment deposition. They can be caused by a change in wind direction, which can be evidence of an ancient desert.

items.title: Ripples
items.sub: suggest a current was present when the sediment was deposited. This could mean an ancient river, stream or sea bed.

items.q: A cliff shows four layers of sedimentary rock. What are these layers called?
In a set of strata, which layer was deposited first?
Ripples found in strata suggest that...
options: a current was present when the sediment was deposited
the sediment was deposited by melting ice only
the rock formed in only a few years

items.q: Which of these is NOT one of the steps that turns sediment into rock?

items: Water in nature always contains minerals.
Sediments are deposited when wind or waterways slow down or when glaciers melt.
Layers of sediment form over many years, leading to compaction.
Sedimentary rock forms when sediment is buried and compressed, and minerals from groundwater cement the grains together.
Strata can be used to create a relative timeline and give clues to the environment when the sediments were deposited.

flashcards.back: A material deposited by water, wind or ice, such as pebbles, sand, or salts left by evaporation.
The process of sediment grains settling out from water or wind as their flow slows, or as ice melts.

flashcards.front: Name three things that cause sediment to be deposited.
flashcards.back: Wind slowing down, water slowing down, and glaciers melting.
Sediment grains are squashed closer together during burial, by the pressure of the layers above.

flashcards.front: What is squeezed out of the sediment during compaction?
flashcards.back: Groundwater that may be between the grains.
Sediment grains are stuck together by minerals deposited from groundwater, turning the sediment into rock.

flashcards.front: How do compaction and cementation differ?
flashcards.back: Compaction is due to pressure. In cementation, mineral crystals act like glue holding the grains together.

flashcards.front: Put the four steps of sedimentary rock formation in order.
flashcards.back: Weathering and erosion, deposition, compaction, cementation.

flashcards.front: About how long does it take for a sedimentary rock to form?

flashcards.back:
Layers of rock formed by the deposition of sediment.

One layer is a stratum.

flashcards.front: In a set of strata, which layers are older?
flashcards.back: The deeper (lower) layers. Higher layers were deposited later.

flashcards.front: What might ripples in strata suggest?
flashcards.back: A current was present when the sediment was deposited, so there might have been an ancient river, stream or sea bed.

flashcards.front: What sedimentary rock does clay form?
flashcards.back:
Shale.

Sand forms sandstone and gravel forms conglomerate.

worksheet.title: Worksheet: Formation of sedimentary rock
worksheet.instructions: Answer each question with a word, a number or a short phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the process of dropping sediments?
questions.explanation: Deposition is the process of sediment grains settling out from water or wind as their flow slows, or as ice melts.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the process that pushes sediment grains closer together?
questions.explanation: Compaction happens because of pressure from the layers above.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the process where mineral crystals glue the grains together?
questions.explanation: Cementation sticks sediment grains together with minerals from groundwater.

questions.prompt: What is the word for one single layer of sedimentary rock (the singular of 'strata')?
questions.explanation: One layer is a stratum and many layers are strata.

questions.prompt: Which sedimentary rock is formed from the sediment sand?
Which sedimentary rock is formed from the sediment clay?
Which sedimentary rock is formed from the sediment gravel?
Chalk is formed from the remains of which tiny living things?
questions.explanation: Chalk is formed from microscopic plankton remains.

questions.prompt: Is a sedimentary rock formed in a few years or in millions of years? Answer with the time it takes.
questions.explanation: There are many steps to making a sedimentary rock, so it takes millions of years.

questions.prompt: In a set of strata, is the highest or the lowest layer the one deposited first?
questions.explanation: Lower strata were deposited earlier, and upper strata were deposited later.
